record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Is the elementary theory of the lattices of ℓ-ideals of ℓ-groups decidable?

evidence.quote: 1.50. Is the elementary theory of the lattices of ℓ-ideals of ℓ-groups decidable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is a group G equipped with a lattice order ≤ such that the group operation is compatible with the order: for all a, b, c, d ∈ G, if a ≤ b then cad ≤ cbd. An ℓ-ideal of an ℓ-group G is a normal convex ℓ-subgroup, that is, a normal subgroup H of G that is also a sublattice of G and is convex in the sense that whenever x ∈ H, y ∈ G, and |y| ≤ |x| (where |z| = z ∨ z⁻¹), we have y ∈ H. The set Id(G) of all ℓ-ideals of G, ordered by inclusion, forms a complete distributive lattice.

To each ℓ-group G associate the lattice Id(G), regarded as a structure in the first-order language of lattices (with binary operations ∧ and ∨). Let 𝓛 be the class of all such lattices Id(G) as G ranges over all ℓ-groups, and let Th(𝓛) be the set of all first-order sentences in the language of lattices that are true in every member of 𝓛.

Question: Is Th(𝓛) decidable? Equivalently, does there exist an algorithm that, given a first-order sentence φ in the language of lattices, decides whether φ holds in the lattice of ℓ-ideals of every ℓ-group?
artifact.status_search_result: For the restricted case of abelian ℓ-groups, the elementary theory of the lattice of ℓ-ideals has been shown to be undecidable (Gurevich/Schwartz-style result published in Algebra and Logic, 2005), giving a negative answer to the analogous problem (Kourovka Notebook 5.20) for abelian ℓ-groups. The general question for arbitrary (not necessarily abelian) ℓ-groups does not appear to be definitively settled in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Elementary Theory for l-Ideal Lattices of Abelian l-Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Elementary theory for ℓ-ideal lattices of Abelian ℓ-groups is shown to be undecidable, providing a negative answer to Problem 5.20 of the Kourovka Notebook.
status_evidence.claim: In the abelian case, the elementary theory of the lattice of ℓ-ideals is undecidable.

status_evidence.title: Lattice Ordered Abelian Groups and Their Model Theory (Tressl)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of model theory of lattice-ordered abelian groups.
status_evidence.claim: Model-theoretic properties of ℓ-groups and their ideal lattices remain an active area.
